title: pytest Gemini: port TestGeminiJourney from bash test script
description:
Port tests/test-gemini-skill-install.sh to tests/integration/test_gemini.py as TestGeminiJourney class following the same pattern as TestClaudeJourney and TestCodexJourney.

Key Gemini differences from Claude/Codex:
- No marketplace registration (Phase 2 N/A)
- Skill install via 'gemini skills link <path> --scope user --consent' (gemini_sub wrapper, no -m flag)
- Skill discovery via 'gemini skills list'
- Agent prompts via: gemini -m gemini-2.5-flash -o text --yolo (with stdin prompt)
- CLAUDECODE / CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT must be unset (clean_env inline like Codex)
- Rules/skills written to .claude/ (same as Claude — Gemini uses Claude rule format)
- Uninstall via: /coding-aegis uninstall helloworld agent prompt
- Cleanup via: gemini skills uninstall coding-aegis --scope user
- Quota errors (MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / 429) must be caught and converted to pytest.skip
- TIMEOUT_LONG = 120 (gemini retries internally, each step can take 60-90s with retries)

Reference files:
- tests/test-gemini-skill-install.sh (source bash test)
- tests/integration/test_codex.py (closest structural match)
- tests/integration/test_claude.py (Claude pattern)
- tests/integration/harness.py (CLIResult, run_cli, assert helpers)
- tests/integration/conftest.py (shared fixtures: repo_root, test_dir)

Acceptance criteria:
- TestGeminiJourney class with class-scoped journey fixture
- Phases: 1 auth, 3 skill linked+listed, 4a detect-tool direct, 4b detect-tool skill, 4c list, 4d show, 5 install helloworld, 5b helloworld responds, 6 uninstall helloworld
- Quota errors → pytest.skip (not fail)
- All phases pass when gemini is on PATH and authenticated
- Module skipped entirely if gemini not on PATH
close_reason: Closed

description:

1. Run: python3 {skill-dir}/detect_tool.py

title: Research Windsurf and Copilot tool detection signals
description:
The current spec (docs/architecture/spec-tool-detection.md) concludes that neither Windsurf nor Copilot inject tool-specific env vars. This needs independent verification before we treat it as settled.

Research questions:
1. Windsurf: Does Cascade set any env vars (WINDSURF_*, CODEIUM_*, or others) when invoking skills or running shell commands? Check community forums, Windsurf GitHub issues, and any open-source Windsurf components.
2. Windsurf: Is ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/ the confirmed global skills path on macOS? Is .windsurf/skills/ the confirmed workspace path?
3. Copilot: Does the Copilot coding agent (GitHub Actions runner) set GITHUB_COPILOT_* or any agent-identity env var? Is GITHUB_ACTIONS=true the only reliable signal?
4. Are there any parent-process signals (process name, socket path) that would survive into a Python subprocess for either tool?

Do NOT implement changes based on this research until findings are reviewed.

title: Design AGENTS.md management strategy for installed packages
description: AGENTS.md is the cross-tool always-on guidance file (recognized by Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf). Currently packages only deliver tool-specific rule files (.claude/rules/, .cursor/rules/, etc.). There is no mechanism for packages to compose sections into AGENTS.md. Questions to resolve: (1) Should packages inject sections into AGENTS.md, or just reference their rules from it? (2) If injecting, how do we manage ownership boundaries between project-authored and governance-managed sections? (3) How do we handle install/uninstall without corrupting the file? (4) Should we use sentinel comments (e.g. <!-- aegis:start --> / <!-- aegis:end -->) or a separate include mechanism? (5) What is the relationship between AGENTS.md guidance and tool-specific rules — are they redundant, complementary, or layered? Create an ADR documenting the decision.
